questions.question: Which of the following raw materials is NOT used to prepare the baking soda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na₂CO₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Baking soda, chemically known as **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)**, is prepared using sodium chloride (NaCl) as a primary raw material.
 
• The **Solvay process** is the most common method for manufacturing baking soda, which involves the reaction of NaCl, NH₃ (ammonia), and CO₂ in water (H₂O).
 
• **Na₂CO₃ (sodium carbonate)**, also known as washing soda, is not directly used in the preparation of baking soda.
 
• Instead, sodium bicarbonate is derived as an intermediate product in the Solvay process, and Na₂CO₃ is formed as the final byproduct, not as a starting raw material.
 
• Therefore, **Na₂CO₃** is not a raw material used in the manufacturing of baking soda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solvay Process:**

 
 
• The Solvay process is an industrial method used to produce sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) and sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃).
 
• It involves the reaction of sodium chloride (NaCl), ammonia (NH₃), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) in water.
 
• The intermediate product, sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), is filtered out and heated to produce Na₂CO₃.
 
 
 
• **Baking Soda (NaHCO₃):**
 
 
• Baking soda is a white crystalline compound used as a leavening agent in baking.
 
• It releases carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas when it reacts with acids or heats, causing baked goods to rise.
 
• It is also widely used for cleaning, deodorizing, and pH regulation in various applications.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃):**
 
 
• Also known as washing soda, it is primarily used in laundry detergents, water softening, and glass manufacturing.
 
• It is not a direct component in the preparation of baking soda but is a final byproduct in the Solvay process.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃):**
 
 
• Ammonia is a key raw material in the Solvay process, playing a crucial role in precipitating sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃).
 
• It is recovered and reused in the process to minimize waste and reduce costs.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):**
 
 
• CO₂ is another essential raw material in the Solvay process, reacting with ammonia and sodium chloride to form sodium bicarbonate.
 
• It ensures the chemical reaction necessary for the production of baking soda.

questions.question: In the South Indian temples, the pyramidal tower is called the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vimana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **vimana** refers to the pyramidal tower that rises above the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha) in South Indian temples.
 
• It is a prominent architectural feature in **Dravidian-style temples**, widely found in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• Unlike the shikhara of North Indian temples, the vimana has a **stepped and gradually tapering structure**.
 
• The vimana often features intricate carvings and sculptures, depicting **mythological stories, deities, and decorative motifs**.
 
• Famous South Indian temples, such as the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, showcase some of the most iconic and towering vimanas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian Architecture:**

 
 
• This style is predominant in South India and is characterized by large temple complexes with **gopurams (ornate entrance towers)** and vimanas.
 
• It originated during the rule of the Pallavas (4th–9th century CE) and flourished under the Cholas, Pandyas, and Vijayanagara empires.
 
 
 
• **Sanctum Sanctorum (Garbhagriha):**
 
 
• The innermost and holiest part of the temple, where the principal deity is enshrined.
 
• The vimana is constructed directly above the garbhagriha, symbolizing the **connection between the earthly and divine realms**.
 
 
 
• **Shikhara vs. Vimana:**
 
 
• While the vimana is used in Dravidian architecture, the term shikhara is used for the curvilinear towers in **Nagara-style temples** of North India.
 
• Both structures serve as focal points of temples but differ in shape, style, and symbolism.
 
 
 
• **Brihadeeswarar Temple:**
 
 
• Located in Tamil Nadu, this UNESCO World Heritage site is a prime example of Dravidian architecture.
 
• Its vimana stands at a height of 66 meters and is one of the tallest temple towers in the world.
 
• The temple was built during the reign of Raja Raja Chola I in the 11th century CE.

questions.question: What is the duration for which a member of a House of Legislature of a State is, without permission of the House, absent from all meetings, thereof the house may declare his seat vacant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A member of the House of Legislature of a State may lose their seat if they are absent from all meetings of the House for **60 days without its permission**.
 
• This provision is governed by **Article 190(4)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The absence is calculated continuously, excluding any period when the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days.
 
• The House must declare the seat vacant through a formal resolution or process to enforce this provision.
 
• The rule ensures **accountability of legislators** and prevents misuse of privileges by absenteeism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 190 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It deals with the **vacation of seats, disqualification, and resignation** of members of the State Legislature.
 
• Clause (4) specifies the conditions under which a seat becomes vacant due to prolonged absenteeism.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Speaker:**
 
 
• The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or the Chairman of the Legislative Council decides on matters related to absenteeism and seat vacancy.
 
• The decision must follow the procedures laid out in the House Rules.
 
 
 
• **Prorogation and Adjournment:**
 
 
• Prorogation refers to the formal ending of a legislative session by the Governor.
 
• Adjournment refers to the suspension of a meeting of the House for a specific period.
 
• Absenteeism during prorogation or long adjournments is not counted towards the 60-day rule.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Provision:**
 
 
• The provision ensures that legislators remain **committed to their responsibilities** and participate in legislative processes.
 
• It prevents wastage of public resources due to non-participation by elected representatives.

questions.question: Who among the following was the famous ruler of the Gauda Kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shashanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shashanka** was the first historical ruler of the Gauda Kingdom, located in present-day Bengal.
 
• He ruled from approximately **590 CE to 625 CE**, and his reign marked the emergence of Bengal as a significant political power.
 
• Shashanka is credited with the **establishment of a unified kingdom in Bengal** and was one of the earliest known kings to embrace Hinduism in the region.
 
• He is often associated with the persecution of Buddhists, including the alleged destruction of the Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya, though this remains a debated topic among historians.
 
• Shashanka's rivalry with **Harsha**, the ruler of Kannauj, is well-documented in historical texts, including the accounts of the Chinese traveler Xuanzang.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gauda Kingdom:**

 
 
• The Gauda Kingdom was an early medieval kingdom centered in Bengal, particularly in the western and northern parts of the region.
 
• It played a critical role in shaping the political and cultural landscape of early medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Harsha:**
 
 
• Harsha was a contemporary of Shashanka and ruled northern India from 606 CE to 647 CE.
 
• He expanded his kingdom significantly but was unable to annex the Gauda Kingdom due to Shashanka's resistance.
 
 
 
• **Xuanzang’s Accounts:**
 
 
• The Chinese traveler Xuanzang visited India during the reign of Harsha and documented the political and cultural dynamics of the time.
 
• He mentioned Shashanka's rule in Bengal and his alleged hostility towards Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Shashanka:**
 
 
• Shashanka is considered a pivotal figure in the history of Bengal, as he laid the foundation for subsequent kingdoms in the region.
 
• His rule marked the beginning of Bengal's prominence in the political history of India.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)?

options.text: Investigating and reporting on financial transactions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Investigating and reporting on financial transactions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is primarily responsible for **auditing and reporting on the financial transactions of the central and state governments.**
 
• The CAG ensures accountability in the use of public funds by thoroughly examining government expenditures and revenues.
 
• Its reports are submitted to the President and Governors, who then present them to the Parliament or State Legislatures for review and action.
 
• The CAG’s role is crucial for maintaining transparency and preventing misuse of public funds.
 
• It audits accounts related to all government departments, public sector enterprises, and other bodies funded by the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Authority:**

 
 
• The CAG is a constitutional authority established under Article 148 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The CAG is independent of the executive to ensure impartiality in auditing government accounts.
 
 
 
• **Reports and Accountability:**
 
 
• The CAG’s reports help the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and other legislative bodies to scrutinize government spending.
 
• Its findings often lead to corrective measures and policy changes to improve financial management.
 
 
 
• **Scope of Audit:**
 
 
• The CAG audits accounts of the central and state governments, public sector undertakings, autonomous bodies, and institutions receiving government grants.
 
• It also conducts performance audits to assess the efficiency and effectiveness of government schemes and projects.
 
 
 
• **International Role:**
 
 
• The CAG of India is a member of the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI).
 
• It contributes to global best practices in public auditing and financial accountability.

questions.question: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phosphorus and Nitrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process where an excessive amount of nutrients leads to rapid growth of algae, commonly referred to as algal blooms, in water bodies.
 
• **Phosphorus (P)** and **Nitrogen (N)** are the two primary nutrients responsible for eutrophication, as they act as fertilizers for algal growth.
 
• Phosphorus is often introduced into water bodies through agricultural runoff containing fertilizers, detergents, and untreated sewage.
 
• Nitrogen primarily enters water systems from sources like fertilizers, livestock waste, and industrial discharges.
 
• The excessive algal growth reduces oxygen levels in the water, leading to the death of aquatic organisms and severely impacting biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Algal Bloom:** A rapid increase or accumulation of algae in water systems, often visible as green, red, or brown discoloration on the water surface.
 
• **Hypoxia:** A condition where the oxygen levels in the water drop drastically due to the decomposition of algae, leading to "dead zones" where aquatic life cannot survive.
 
• **Sources of Nutrients:** Nutrient pollution is primarily caused by agricultural runoff, urban wastewater, industrial discharges, and improper disposal of fertilizers and detergents.
 
• **Impact on Ecosystems:** Eutrophication leads to biodiversity loss, disruption of food chains, and contamination of drinking water sources due to toxins produced by certain algal species.
 
• **Preventive Measures:** Managing agricultural practices, reducing fertilizer use, treating wastewater, and creating buffer zones near water bodies can help control eutrophication.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.

options.text: The development of the cotton textile industry in Britain led to the decline of Indian textile producers.
Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century.
The Sale and Devang communities of South India were famous for weaving.
The first cotton textile mill in India was established in Bombay in 1854.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decline of Indian textile producers began with the industrial revolution in Britain, leading to the development of its cotton textile industry.
 
• The statement that "Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century" is incorrect as Indian textiles had already lost significant ground by the 19th century due to British policies and industrialization.
 
• The Sale and Devang communities of South India were historically renowned for their expertise in weaving, contributing significantly to India's textile heritage.
 
• The first cotton textile mill in India was indeed established in Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1854, marking the start of India's modern textile industry.
 
• British policies, including high import duties on Indian textiles and the influx of machine-made British goods, caused a decline in India's handloom industry during colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Revolution and Indian Textiles:**

 
 
• The Industrial Revolution in Britain in the late 18th century introduced mechanized textile production, reducing the global demand for Indian handcrafted textiles.
 
• British manufacturers produced cheaper machine-made textiles, which were exported globally, outcompeting Indian products.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Policies Impacting Indian Textiles:**
 
 
• High import tariffs on Indian textiles in Britain and low tariffs on British goods in India created an unequal trade environment.
 
• The British colonial government promoted the export of raw cotton from India to feed British mills, further damaging India's textile industry.
 
 
 
• **Indian Handloom Communities:**
 
 
• Sale and Devang communities in South India were historically known for their weaving skills, producing exquisite textiles such as silk and cotton fabrics.
 
• Other weaving communities across India, including those in Bengal and Gujarat, were also heavily impacted by British colonial policies.
 
 
 
• **Modern Textile Industry in India:**
 
 
• The establishment of textile mills in Bombay in 1854 marked the beginning of India's modern textile industry.
 
• Despite the colonial setbacks, India's textile industry has grown significantly post-independence, becoming a major global player.

questions.question: The famous Jain temple of Dilwara, built by Solanki rulers, is located at which place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mount Abu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dilwara Temples are a group of **Jain temples** located in **Mount Abu**, Rajasthan, India, renowned for their exquisite marble architecture and intricate craftsmanship.
 
• These temples were built between the **11th and 13th centuries** by the Solanki rulers and dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras (spiritual teachers).
 
• There are five prominent temples at Dilwara: **Vimal Vasahi, Luna Vasahi, Pittalhar, Parshvanatha, and Mahavir Swami**, each known for its unique architectural beauty.
 
• The **Vimal Vasahi Temple**, dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, Adinath, is the oldest and most elaborate, constructed in 1031 AD by Vimal Shah, a minister of the Solanki dynasty.
 
• The temples are particularly famous for their **intricate marble carvings**, including ceilings, pillars, and doorways, showcasing unparalleled artistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mount Abu** is a popular hill station in Rajasthan and the only one in the state, located in the Aravalli Range. It is known for its scenic beauty and historical significance.
 
• The **Solanki dynasty**, also known as the Chaulukya dynasty, was a prominent ruling dynasty in Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan during the medieval period, known for their patronage of art and architecture.
 
• Jainism is an ancient Indian religion known for its emphasis on **non-violence (Ahimsa)**, asceticism, and the pursuit of spiritual liberation through self-discipline and meditation.
 
• The Dilwara temples serve as an important pilgrimage site for Jains and are also admired by art enthusiasts and historians for their architectural brilliance.
 
• Mount Abu is also home to other attractions like the **Nakki Lake** and the **Achalgarh Fort**, making it a significant tourist destination.

questions.question: In December 2023, which former Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) CEO and MD joined the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay) as Head of Translational Research and Entrepreneurship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajesh Gopinathan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rajesh Gopinathan**, the former CEO and MD of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), joined IIT Bombay in December 2023 as the **Head of Translational Research and Entrepreneurship.**
 
• He served as the CEO and MD of TCS from **February 2017 to March 2023**, leading the company to significant global growth.
 
• His new role at IIT Bombay focuses on promoting **translational research** and supporting entrepreneurial ventures, aligning academic innovations with industrial applications.
 
• The initiative aims to strengthen IIT Bombay's commitment to fostering innovation and bridging the gap between research and commercialization.
 
• Rajesh Gopinathan is an alumnus of IIM Ahmedabad and NIT Trichy, and his leadership experience is expected to greatly benefit the institution’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Translational Research**

 
 
• It involves the process of applying findings from basic scientific research to develop practical solutions for real-world problems.
 
• The goal is to bridge the gap between laboratory discoveries and their implementation in industries or healthcare systems.
 
• This approach is widely used in fields like biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and engineering innovations.
 
 
 
• **Entrepreneurship at IITs**
 
 
• Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) are increasingly focusing on fostering entrepreneurship through incubators and innovation hubs.
 
• Many IITs have established entrepreneurial cells (E-cells) and technology business incubators (TBIs) to support start-ups.
 
• These initiatives provide mentorship, funding, and infrastructure to aspiring entrepreneurs.
 
 
 
• **Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)**
 
 
• TCS is a global leader in IT services, consulting, and business solutions, and is part of the Tata Group.
 
• Under Rajesh Gopinathan’s leadership, TCS became one of the most valuable IT service brands globally.
 
• It operates in over 46 countries and offers services across industries such as healthcare, finance, and retail.
 
 
 
• **IIT Bombay**
 
 
• IIT Bombay is one of India’s premier engineering and technology institutions, established in 1958.
 
• It is renowned for its academic excellence and contributions to research and innovation.
 
• The institution has a strong focus on fostering start-ups and bridging the gap between academia and industry.

questions.question: 'Dollu Kunitha' is primarily a folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Dollu Kunitha'** is a traditional folk dance form that originated in the state of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• This dance is primarily performed by men of the **Kuruba community** and revolves around rhythmic beats produced by large drums called **'Dollu'**.
 
• The dance is a vibrant combination of **percussion, music, and synchronized movements**, often performed during religious festivals and cultural events.
 
• 'Dollu Kunitha' typically portrays mythological themes and stories, especially those associated with **Lord Shiva** and his devotees.
 
• The performers wear traditional attire and engage in energetic movements, creating a visually captivating and spiritually uplifting experience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuruba Community:**

 
 
• The Kuruba community, a prominent shepherd caste in Karnataka, has a strong cultural and historical association with 'Dollu Kunitha'.
 
• This community traditionally worships **Lord Beereshwara**, a form of Lord Shiva, and their folklore often inspires the dance.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Instruments:**
 
 
• The primary instrument used in 'Dollu Kunitha' is the **Dollu drum**, made of wood and buffalo hide for producing deep, resonant sounds.
 
• The accompanying instruments include cymbals and wind instruments to enhance the musical harmony.
 
 
 
• **Performance Settings:**
 
 
• The dance is performed in open spaces, temple courtyards, or during village festivals.
 
• It is also showcased in cultural programs to promote Karnataka's rich heritage.
 
 
 
• **Other Folk Dances of Karnataka:**
 
 
• Besides 'Dollu Kunitha', Karnataka is also home to other folk dances such as **Yakshagana**, **Veeragase**, and **Kamsale**.
 
• These dances reflect the state's diverse culture and artistic excellence.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first President of Indian National congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Womesh Chandra Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Womesh Chandra Banerjee was the **first President of the Indian National Congress**, which was established in 1885.
 
• The **first session of the Indian National Congress** was held in **Bombay (now Mumbai)** from 28 to 31 December 1885.
 
• He presided over the **first session of INC**, which was attended by 72 delegates from across the country.
 
• The Indian National Congress was founded by **A.O. Hume**, a retired British civil servant, to create a platform for civil and political dialogue among educated Indians.
 
• Womesh Chandra Banerjee was a prominent barrister and an influential leader during the early days of the freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC):**

 
 
• The INC was established in 1885 with the aim of obtaining a greater share in government for educated Indians.
 
• It later became a pivotal organization in the Indian independence movement against British colonial rule.
 
• The INC played a major role in mobilizing public opinion and organizing protests and campaigns for independence.
 
 
 
• **A.O. Hume:**
 
 
• Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, was instrumental in the formation of the INC.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of the Indian National Congress."
 
• Hume's vision was to provide a platform for Indians to express their grievances and aspirations peacefully.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Presidents of INC:**
 
 
• After Womesh Chandra Banerjee, other prominent leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji, George Yule, and Badruddin Tyabji served as presidents of the INC.
 
• George Yule was the first non-Indian to preside over the Congress in 1888.
 
 
 
• **Early Objectives of INC:**
 
 
• To promote friendly relations among nationalist political workers from different parts of the country.
 
• To develop and consolidate feelings of national unity irrespective of caste, religion, or province.
 
• To formulate popular demands and present them before the British government in a peaceful manner.

questions.question: Which of the following States/Union Territories is included in the 'Areas of Inadequate Rainfall' of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ladakh is a Union Territory in India that is characterized by an arid, cold desert climate due to its location in the Himalayan rain shadow region.
 
• It receives very low annual precipitation, often less than 50 mm, making it one of the areas with inadequate rainfall in India.
 
• The region's unique geography includes high-altitude plateaus and mountains, which obstruct the monsoon winds, further reducing rainfall.
 
• The scarcity of rainfall has led to the reliance on glacier meltwater for agriculture and other water needs in Ladakh.
 
• Efforts are being made to address water scarcity in Ladakh through innovative methods like artificial glaciers and community water management projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Areas of Inadequate Rainfall:**

 
 
• Regions categorized under inadequate rainfall generally receive less than 750 mm of annual rainfall.
 
• These areas include parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Ladakh, and some regions in the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Rain Shadow Effect:**
 
 
• Occurs when mountains block the passage of rain-producing weather systems, causing arid conditions on the leeward side.
 
• Ladakh is an example of a rain shadow region due to its location beyond the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Glacier Meltwater Dependency:**
 
 
• Ladakh relies heavily on meltwater from glaciers for irrigation and drinking water.
 
• Climate change is impacting glacier size and meltwater availability, posing challenges to water security.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Glacier Technology:**
 
 
• An innovative water conservation method pioneered by Sonam Wangchuk in Ladakh.
 
• Artificial glaciers store water during winter and release it during summer for agricultural use.

questions.question: In the year 2010, Commonwealth Games was hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Commonwealth Games of 2010 were hosted by **India**, and the games were held in the capital city, **New Delhi**.
 
• It was the **19th edition** of the Commonwealth Games and took place from **3rd October to 14th October 2010**.
 
• India became the **third developing country** to host the Commonwealth Games, after Jamaica (1966) and Malaysia (1998).
 
• The event witnessed participation from **71 nations** and territories, with over 6,000 athletes competing in various disciplines.
 
• India achieved its **best-ever performance** in the history of the Commonwealth Games, finishing second in the medal tally with a total of **101 medals** (38 Gold, 27 Silver, and 36 Bronze).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commonwealth Games Overview**

 
 
• The Commonwealth Games is a multinational, multi-sport event organized every four years for athletes from the Commonwealth of Nations.
 
• The event was first held in 1930 and is often referred to as the "Friendly Games."
 
• It features various sports, including athletics, swimming, badminton, hockey, and wrestling, among others.
 
 
 
• **2010 Commonwealth Games Venues**
 
 
• The main venue for the event was the **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** in New Delhi.
 
• Other prominent venues included the Indira Gandhi Arena, Siri Fort Sports Complex, and Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range.
 
 
 
• **Theme and Mascot**
 
 
• The theme song for the 2010 Commonwealth Games was "**Jiyo Utho Bado Jeeto**" composed by A.R. Rahman.
 
• The official mascot was **Shera**, a tiger symbolizing India’s cultural heritage and the spirit of sportsmanship.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Infrastructure Impact**

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of rural population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, **Bihar recorded the highest percentage of rural population** among all Indian states.
 
• Approximately **88.7% of Bihar's total population** resides in rural areas, making it the most rural state in India.
 
• This high rural population is attributed to the state's predominantly agrarian economy and lack of significant urbanization.
 
• Other states with high rural population percentages include Uttar Pradesh, Assam, and Odisha, but **Bihar leads in terms of proportion**.
 
• The rural population in India as a whole was recorded at **68.84% in the 2011 Census**, highlighting the country's rural demographic dominance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rural Population:**

 
 
• Rural population refers to people living in villages and smaller settlements as opposed to urban areas (cities and towns).
 
• Rural areas in India are characterized by low population density, reliance on agriculture, and limited infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Census of India 2011:**
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years and provides comprehensive data on population, literacy, employment, and living conditions.
 
• In 2011, the total population of India was recorded at **1.21 billion**, with 68.84% living in rural areas and 31.16% in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in India:**
 
 
• Urbanization refers to the process by which rural areas transform into urban settlements through industrialization and modernization.
 
• India's urbanization rate is increasing, with significant migration to cities for better employment, education, and healthcare opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Agrarian Economy of Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar's economy is heavily reliant on agriculture, with crops like rice, wheat, and maize being staples.
 
• The lack of significant industrialization has contributed to the state's high rural population percentage.

questions.question: The Parliamentary form of Government is a key feature given in the Indian Constitution and its provisions are detailed in Articles ___________ of Part V (Chapter II).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**79 to 122**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Parliamentary form of Government is a fundamental feature of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Provisions related to the Union Executive, including the President, Vice President, Council of Ministers, and the Prime Minister, are detailed in **Articles 79 to 122** under Part V (Chapter II) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 79 establishes the Parliament of India, which consists of the President and the two Houses – the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• Article 74 specifies that the President acts in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This framework ensures collective responsibility, a defining principle of the Parliamentary system of governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary System:**

 
 
• The Parliamentary system is modeled on the British system and emphasizes the fusion of powers between the executive and the legislature.
 
• It is characterized by the accountability of the executive (Council of Ministers) to the legislature (Parliament).
 
 
 
• **Key Articles in Part V:**
 
 
• Article 79: Constitution of Parliament (President, Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha).
 
• Article 85: Sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution.
 
• Article 100: Voting in Houses, quorum, and decisions.
 
• Article 110: Definition of Money Bills.
 
 
 
• **Collective Responsibility:**
 
 
• As per Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• This ensures the democratic accountability of the executive to the legislature.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• While India follows a Parliamentary system, there is a functional separation of powers between the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary to maintain checks and balances.

questions.question: Hampi Utsava is a colourful cultural festival that emulates the ethos and grandeur of which of the following empires?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayanagara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hampi Utsava, also known as Hampi Festival, celebrates the **rich cultural heritage** of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The festival is held annually in Hampi, Karnataka, which was the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• It features various events including traditional dance, music performances, and vibrant processions to emulate the grandeur of the Vijayanagara rulers.
 
• Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of India's most significant archaeological and historical landmarks.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646 CE) is known for its advancements in art, architecture, and administration, with monuments like Virupaksha Temple and Vittala Temple being prime examples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE by Harihara and Bukka Raya of the Sangama dynasty.
 
• It was one of the largest and most powerful empires in Indian history, known for its contributions to culture, architecture, and trade.
 
• Key architectural achievements include the construction of temples, step wells, and markets, showcasing Dravidian and Indo-Islamic styles.
 
• The empire served as a stronghold against invasions by the Delhi Sultanate and ensured the preservation of South Indian traditions.
 
 
 
• **Hampi:**
 
 
• Hampi is located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in Karnataka and is renowned for its historical significance.
 
• The site contains over 1,600 monuments spread across 41.5 square kilometers, including temples, forts, and royal complexes.
 
• It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986 due to its cultural and architectural importance.
 
 
 
• **Hampi Utsava:**
 
 
• The festival is organized by the Karnataka government to promote tourism and preserve the legacy of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Events include puppet shows, fireworks, exhibitions, and performances by folk artists.
 
• The festival attracts thousands of visitors, both domestic and international, contributing to the local economy.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**
 
 
• India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including cultural, natural, and mixed sites.
 
• Prominent examples include the Taj Mahal, Jaipur City, Ajanta Caves, and Kaziranga National Park.
 
• These sites represent India's rich cultural and natural diversity on the global stage.

questions.question: Which of the following is a molecular compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CO₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CO₂ (Carbon Dioxide)** is a molecular compound because it is formed by covalent bonding between carbon and oxygen atoms.
 
• Molecular compounds are typically composed of nonmetals. CO₂ consists of two nonmetals: carbon and oxygen.
 
• The carbon atom in CO₂ shares its electrons with two oxygen atoms, forming double covalent bonds, which is characteristic of molecular compounds.
 
• CO₂ exists as discrete molecules in its gaseous state, unlike ionic compounds which form a lattice structure.
 
• It is not an ionic compound like NaCl or MgSO₄, which are composed of ions, nor a metallic compound like CaO.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Compounds:**

 
 
• Molecular compounds are made of nonmetals and are held together by covalent bonds, where electrons are shared between atoms.
 
• They typically have lower melting and boiling points compared to ionic compounds.
 
• Examples include CO₂, H₂O, and CH₄.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Compounds:**
 
 
• Ionic compounds are formed by the transfer of electrons between metals and nonmetals, resulting in positive and negative ions.
 
• Examples include NaCl, MgSO₄, and CaO.
 
• They usually have high melting and boiling points and form a crystal lattice structure.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):**
 
 
• CO₂ is a greenhouse gas that is a major contributor to global warming and climate change.
 
• It is released through natural processes such as respiration and volcanic eruptions, as well as human activities like burning fossil fuels.
 
• It is used in various applications, including carbonated beverages, fire extinguishers, and as a refrigerant.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• Commonly known as quicklime, it is an ionic compound formed by calcium and oxygen.
 
• It is used in cement production, soil stabilization, and as a chemical reagent.

questions.question: In India, documented by a study, in which level of education is the majority of the population unemployed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graduate and post-graduate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has a unique unemployment trend where **graduates and post-graduates face higher unemployment rates** compared to individuals with lower educational qualifications.
 
• The primary reason is a **mismatch between the skills acquired through higher education and the demands of the job market**.
 
• According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2022-23, the unemployment rate for highly educated individuals is significantly higher than for those with basic or vocational skills.
 
• The **lack of industry-relevant courses** and limited job opportunities in specialized sectors contribute to this trend.
 
• In contrast, those with primary or middle school education often take up **low-skilled jobs in the informal sector**, leading to lower unemployment rates in those categories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unemployment Rate in India**

 
 
• The unemployment rate is defined as the percentage of the labor force that is unemployed but actively seeking employment.
 
• The **PLFS** provides annual and quarterly estimates of employment and unemployment in India.
 
• India's overall unemployment rate was reported at **4.1% in 2022-23**, with significant variations across education levels.
 
 
 
• **Types of Unemployment in India**
 
 
• **Structural Unemployment:** Caused by a mismatch between job skills and market demands.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment:** Temporary unemployment during job transitions.
 
• **Disguised Unemployment:** Common in agriculture, where more people are employed than needed.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Address Unemployment**
 
 
• **Skill India:** Aims to train over 40 crore individuals in industry-relevant skills by 2022.
 
• **Startup India:** Promotes entrepreneurship by providing funding, mentorship, and tax benefits.
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** Focuses on self-reliance and job creation in various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Unemployment**
 
 
• High unemployment among educated individuals can lead to **economic inefficiency** and social unrest.
 
• It also contributes to **brain drain**, as skilled individuals seek opportunities abroad.

• Balamuralikrishna performed extensively across India and globally, earning critical acclaim for his unique style and technical mastery in Carnatic music.

• **Carnatic Music:**

questions.question: Which of the following are edible polysaccharides?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch, alginates, pectins and chitosans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Starch**: A widely consumed edible polysaccharide found in staple foods such as rice, wheat, maize, and potatoes. It serves as a primary energy source for humans.
 
• **Alginates**: Polysaccharides extracted from brown seaweeds, commonly used as a food additive for thickening, gelling, and stabilizing in products like ice cream and sauces.
 
• **Pectins**: Naturally occurring polysaccharides in fruits such as apples and citrus, often used in jams and jellies as a gelling agent.
 
• **Chitosans**: Derived from chitin, these are edible and are increasingly used in the food industry for their potential health benefits and preservation properties.
 
• These polysaccharides are considered safe for human consumption and widely used in the food industry for their functional properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polysaccharides**: Complex carbohydrates made up of long chains of monosaccharide units. They serve various functions such as energy storage (starch, glycogen) and structural components (cellulose, chitin).
 
• **Chitin**: A structural polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods and fungal cell walls. While non-edible in its raw form, its derivative, chitosan, is edible and used in food processing.
 
• **Cellulose**: A structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls. Though indigestible by humans, it serves as dietary fiber, aiding in digestion.
 
• **Food Additives**: Polysaccharides like alginates and pectins are often used as food additives due to their gelling, stabilizing, and thickening properties.
 
• **Nutritional Importance**: Edible polysaccharides like starch are vital for providing energy, whereas others like pectins and chitosans contribute to functional food properties, promoting health and wellness.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Hungry Tide'?

• Ghosh has received multiple awards, including the **Padma Shri** (2007) and the **Jnanpith Award** (2018), India's highest literary honor.

questions.question: Odissi dancer ________ was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2022 in the dance category.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Niranjan Rout**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Niranjan Rout**, an eminent Odissi dancer, was awarded the prestigious **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2022** in the dance category.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards are conferred by the **National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama** in India.
 
• The award recognizes individuals for their exceptional contribution to the performing arts and is considered one of the highest honors in the field.
 
• **Odissi** is one of the oldest classical dance forms originating from Odisha and is characterized by its intricate footwork, graceful movements, and emotive expressions.
 
• Niranjan Rout has been a prominent figure in the Odissi dance community, contributing significantly to preserving and promoting this classical art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**

 
 
• Established in **1952**, the Akademi functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
• The awards are aimed at recognizing and honoring artists for their lifetime achievements in music, dance, drama, and other performing arts.
 
• Recipients are selected by a panel of experts based on their contribution to their respective fields.
 
 
 
• **Odissi Dance**
 
 
• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India as recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• It has its roots in the **temple dances** performed as a form of devotion to deities, particularly Lord Jagannath.
 
• The dance involves unique postures like the **Tribhangi** (three-bend position) and intricate gestures (Mudras).
 
• Odissi is known for its lyrical grace and the ability to depict a wide range of emotions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• The award includes a citation, an angavastram (shawl), and a cash prize of Rs. 1,00,000.
 
• It highlights India's rich cultural heritage and encourages artists to continue their work in preserving traditional art forms.
